hep-ph.author: Ashis Tamang, Nishal Rai, Javier Esteban, Eugenio Megias
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ and $\Delta=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

hep-ph.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
hep-ph.author: Oliver H. E. Philcox
hep-ph.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $\sigma_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

hep-ph.title: Looking for WIMPs through the neutrino fogs
hep-ph.author: Itay M. Bloch, Salvatore Bottaro, Diego Redigolo, Ludovico Vittorio
hep-ph.abstract: We revisit the expected sensitivity of large-scale xenon detectors to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). Assuming current primary noise sources can be mitigated, we find that with the present discrimination power between nuclear and electron recoils, the experimental sensitivity is limited not only by atmospheric neutrinos' nuclear recoils (''nuclear recoil neutrino fog'') but also by solar neutrinos' electron-recoil events (''electron recoil neutrino fog''). While this is known by experimentalists, it is often missed or misunderstood by theorists, and we therefore emphasize this effect. We set up a realistic detector simulation to quantify the contamination of the WIMP signal from both these neutrino backgrounds. We observe that the electron-recoil background remains significant even for signal rates exceeding those of atmospheric neutrinos, as predicted by most electroweak WIMP candidates. We update the projections for the required exposure to exclude/discover a given electroweak WIMP, streamlining the computation of their signal rates and uncertainties. We show that all of the real WIMPs with zero hypercharge can be excluded (discovered) with a 50 tonne year (300 tonne year) exposure. A similar exposure will allow to probe a large portion of the viable parameter space for complex WIMP with non-zero hypercharge.

hep-ph.title: Quark and lepton mixing in the asymptotically safe Standard Model
hep-ph.author: Astrid Eichhorn, Zois Gyftopoulos, Aaron Held
hep-ph.abstract: The quark mixing (CKM) matrix is near-diagonal, whereas the lepton mixing (PMNS) matrix is not. We learn that both observations can generically be explained within an ultraviolet completion of the Standard Model with gravity. This ultraviolet completion results in approximate relations between CKM matrix elements. The accuracy with which these hold translates into the length of asymptotically safe scaling regimes. Experimental data are consistent with the theoretical expectations arising from a fixed-point cascade at transplanckian scales. Similar results would hold for the PMNS matrix if neutrino Yukawa couplings were large. The ultraviolet complete theory, therefore, must -- and in fact can -- avoid such an outcome. It achieves this through a dynamical mechanism that limits the size of neutrino Yukawa couplings. Thus, large neutrino mixing is intimately tied to small Dirac neutrino masses, $\sum m_{\nu} \lesssim O(1)\, \rm eV$, and a mass gap in the Standard Model fermion masses.

hep-ph.title: Scalar nonstandard neutrino interactions in galactic supernovae
hep-ph.author: Bhaskar Dutta, Aparajitha Karthikeyan, Nityasa Mishra, Yago Porto, Louis E. Strigari
hep-ph.abstract: We analyze the prospects for studying scalar nonstandard interactions (SNSI) using the neutrino burst from a galactic supernova (SN). SNSI modifies the resonant flavor conversion and, correspondingly, the neutronization burst signal, and may be identifiable in future multi-tonne-scale experiments, such as Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Notably, in the normal mass ordering, SNSI can lead to an anomalous (re)appearance of the neutronization-burst $\nu_e$ peak at Earth, a feature otherwise strongly suppressed in the Standard Model. We show that, in the presence of SNSI, neutrinos propagating out of the dense SN environment acquire a density-squared-dependent contribution to their mass-squared differences, which in turn modifies the energy levels of the neutrino matter eigenstates. This density-squared effect is absent in less dense environments such as the Earth or the Sun and is precisely what enables SN neutrinos to probe SNSI parameters up to 4 orders of magnitude below the values accessible to solar or terrestrial neutrino sources.

hep-ph.title: Prominence: A discriminator of gravitational wave signals
hep-ph.author: João Gonçalves, Danny Marfatia, António P. Morais
hep-ph.abstract: The concept of prominence is familiar to signal engineers, topographers and mountaineers. We introduce Prominence $\cal P$ as a discriminator of gravitational wave (GW) signals. We treat black hole and neutron star binaries as astrophysical background sources, and show how $\cal P$ can be used to distinguish between GW spectra produced by first-order phase transitions, domain walls and cosmic strings, and combinations thereof. Prominence can also be used to discriminate between these and off-piste sources of GWs. The uncertainty in the measured energy density in GWs at Pulsar Timing Arrays needs to be at the sub-percent to percent level for $\cal{P}$ to achieve discrimination at 3$\sigma$. LISA and ET data are expected to have sufficiently small uncertainties that Prominence can play a central role in their analysis. We define and apply a $\chi^2$ statistic based on an inner product in signal space to show that sources indistinguishable at $2\sigma$ using the signal-to-noise ratio can be distinguished using $\mathcal{P}$ with significances above and in some cases far above $3\sigma$.

hep-ph.title: Stringent constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions using high-purity $ν_μ$ CC events in IceCube DeepCore
hep-ph.author: J Krishnamoorthi, Anil Kumar, Sanjib Kumar Agarwalla
hep-ph.abstract: The neutral-current (NC) nonstandard interactions (NSIs) of neutrinos with fermions can modify the flavor oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos as they propagate through the Earth. We present constraints on the NC-NSI parameters $\varepsilon_{\mu\tau}$ and $\varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu}$ (one at a time) using a high-purity sample of $\nu_{\mu}$ charged-current atmospheric neutrino events collected by IceCube DeepCore over 7.5 years of livetime. These two parameters significantly affect the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance channel for which this golden event sample is optimized by IceCube Collaboration. The best fit to this dataset is consistent with no NSI hypothesis, and we place the stringent constraints $-\,0.0094 < \varepsilon_{\mu\tau} < 0.0079$ and $-\,0.031 < \varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu} < 0.029$ at the 90% confidence level, assuming normal mass ordering.

hep-ph.title: Metastable cosmic strings are broken at the start
hep-ph.author: Lorenzo Tranchedone, Ethan Carragher, Edward Hardy, Natálie Koscelanská van IJcken
hep-ph.abstract: We show that metastable cosmic strings break at early times, either via finite-temperature effects or by attaching to pre-existing monopoles during network percolation. The resulting segments can be initially super-horizon in size and thus persist for a significant amount of time. If the strings do not re-percolate, the network's eventual destruction is typically due to this early-time breaking rather than late-time quantum tunnelling. Survival of strings to epochs probed by NANOGrav requires $m_M^2/\mu\gtrsim 10^3$, where $m_M$ and $\mu$ are the monopole mass and the string tension respectively, over an order of magnitude larger than previous estimates. We also revisit quantum-tunnelling induced breaking. Results from numerical simulations suggest that this occurs mainly at rare high-tension points on the strings, yielding a rate much larger than is usually assumed. We briefly discuss the related scenario of flux tubes in a dark QCD-like hidden sector with dark-quark masses above the confinement scale.

hep-ph.title: Fermion scattering in a Bose-Einstein condensate
hep-ph.author: César E. Echevarría, José F. Nieves, Francisco Orbe, Sarira Sahu
hep-ph.abstract: In a recent work, we considered the propagation of fermions in the background of a scalar Bose-Einstein (BE) condensate. Using some illustrative Yukawa-type coupling models between the fermions and the scalar fields, we determined the dispersion relations of the fermions and the scalar modes in various models. To complement that work, here we consider the corresponding fermion spinors and propagators, which are required for the calculation of rates of processes involving the fermions, as well as the thermal, and/or higher order, corrections to such rates. We obtain and present here concise formulas which are useful for those applications. As an application and for illustrative purposes we specifically calculate the rate for a generic fermion (which we denote by $\chi$) with the fermions in the BE background, using commonly used models for the fermion interactions. Due to the fact that the background fermion dispersion relations are helicity dependent, the kinematics have some unique and non-standard features. For example, at a particular value of the momentum one of the fermion modes has zero group velocity, which leads to a singularity in the scattering rate of the type of the Van Hove singularity in the density of states of some condensed matter systems. The results of the framework presented here, besides their merit in their own right, can be useful in specific contexts and applications, such as cosmic-ray electron cooling through dark matter-electron scattering, and similar ones involving neutrino and/or electron propagation in a scalar Dark Matter background.

hep-ph.title: PINNs for Solving Two-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations in Vacuum and Matter Environments for Atmospheric and Reactor Neutrinos: A detailed analysis
hep-ph.author: Srinivasan T., Kalyani Desikan
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrino oscillations provide crucial insights into fundamental particle physics, with two-flavor approximations offering a robust framework for analyzing reactor and atmospheric phenomena. Currently, standard numerical integrators represent the gold standard for solving the associated evolution equations, achieving machine precision at negligible computational cost. However, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as a powerful surrogate model for handling high-dimensional systems, complex geometries, and inverse parameter estimation. In this paper, we establish a foundational proof-of-concept by applying PINNs to solve the coupled ordinary differential equations governing neutrino evolution in vacuum and constant-density matter profiles. We also discuss the theoretical framework encompassing vacuum mixing and the matter enhanced neutrino oscillations and rigorously benchmark the PINNs against standard NuFast and RK4 (Runge-Kutta 4) solutions. By carefully optimizing our network architecture, we demonstrate that PINNs can achieve high-precision agreement with experimental standards for reactor (low-energy) and atmospheric (high-energy) neutrinos, which we use as our case study. This paper evaluates the robustness of the PINNs approach through a comprehensive error analysis, establishing a baseline validation for its application to more challenging problems in neutrino physics, such as variable density profiles.

hep-ph.title: On the magnetic counterpart of the Uehling correction
hep-ph.author: T. Azevedo, F.A. Barone, C. Farina, R. de Melo e Souza, G. Zarpelon
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we investigate the magnetic properties of the quantum vacuum in the context of QED. We calculate the quantum relativistic correction of virtual particle-anti-particle pair creation to the field of a classical point-like idealized magnet. Using such correction, we find the induced currents stemming from the effect of the polarization of the vacuum, which behaves like a paramagnetic medium. We also calculate the correction to the electric dipole potential and show that the well-known symmetry between the classical fields of point electric and magnetic dipoles is broken at the quantum level. Lastly, to illustrate possible applications of our findings, we briefly discuss the effect of the corrections obtained here in the context of neutron-neutron scattering and the hyperfine splitting for hydrogen-like atoms.

hep-ph.title: Real versus Complex Fermion Bare Mass and Multi-Wall String Defect Annihilation
hep-ph.author: Utsav Atta, Tathagata Ghosh, Sudip Manna
hep-ph.abstract: Particle physics models beyond the Standard Model often contain global symmetries to address various unanswered questions. However, a common criticism of theories based on global symmetries is that such symmetries are generally expected to be explicitly violated by gravitational effects at the Planck scale. In the case of a global $U(1)$ symmetry, this explicit breaking can reduce the symmetry to a discrete subgroup of $U(1)$, leading to the formation of cosmic strings attached to multiple domain walls (DWs). These DWs are usually cosmologically problematic, since their slow scaling behavior can eventually dominate the energy density of the Universe, giving rise to the well-known cosmological DW problem, which is strongly constrained by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. In this work, we propose a mechanism for the annihilation of these DWs. If a fermion coupled to the symmetry-breaking scalar has a small bare mass, radiative corrections generate a temperature-dependent vacuum bias that drives DW collapse. As an example, we consider a majoron model with right-handed neutrinos, where gravity-induced operators produce a string-wall network. We show that a real bare Majorana mass is sufficient to induce complete DW annihilation for even-dimensional gravity-induced operators, whereas odd-dimensional operators require a complex bare Majorana mass whose phase lifts the residual vacuum degeneracy, enabling complete annihilation.

hep-ph.title: Particle production from bubble collisions
hep-ph.author: Anish Ghoshal, Pratyay Pal, Alessandro Strumia
hep-ph.abstract: Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.

hep-ph.title: From Gradient Postulates to Gauge Structure: Chirality, Conserved Charges, and Constraints on Internal Symmetry
hep-ph.author: Xinqiao Li
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a conceptual framework in which, in the non-relativistic static limit, conservative forces arise as gradients of guidance potentials, and the charges that generate these potentials are conserved and form a Lie algebra. We examine what constraints these postulates, together with the empirical facts of parity violation and non-Abelian weak isospin, impose on the internal symmetry group of a gauge theory. We argue that the non-Abelian character of the gauge sector follows from the conserved-charge algebra together with the observed non-Abelian weak isospin algebra. The requirement that the internal group accommodate chiral fermions constrains the admissible representations. Classical stability, charge quantization, and anomaly cancellation provide three physical consistency conditions that strongly constrain the internal group to be compact. With a minimality criterion, the Standard Model group emerges as the minimal candidate among a small set of compact anomaly-free groups with chiral content. We explicitly identify the minimality criterion as a selective assumption rather than a derived result. We do not claim a unique derivation of the Standard Model group. We also show that the scalar guidance potential reproduces Newtonian gravity and Coulomb's law in the non-relativistic limit, and that relativistic consistency requires its upgrade to a metric tensor and gauge vector fields. The postulates substantially constrain the space of viable gauge theories and provide a conceptual basis for treating the gauge group as a constrained rather than arbitrary input.

hep-ph.title: Probing Lepton-Flavor-Violating Four-Lepton Operators at a Muon Collider
hep-ph.author: Sukanta Dutta, Purnath Unnikrishnan, Yashasvi
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate charged lepton-flavor violation (LFV) induced by dimension-six four-lepton operators within the Standard Model effective field theory(SMEFT) at a proposed high-energy muon collider. We study the processes $\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\to e^{\pm}\tau^{\mp}$, $\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\to e^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$, and $\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\to \mu^{\pm}\tau^{\mp}$ at $\sqrt{s}=3$, $10$, and $14$~TeV, incorporating beam polarization and hadronic $\tau$ reconstruction. Using an optimal-observable analysis of the angular distributions, we perform a global fit to the relevant set of four-lepton operators. Projected sensitivities reach $C/\Lambda^{2}\sim(0.5-1.2) \times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$, depending on the flavor and chiral structure of the operator, exceeding current limits by up to an order of magnitude. A combined analysis of multiple center-of-mass energies and beam polarizations significantly improves the resolution of correlations among the Wilson coefficients. These results highlight the strong sensitivity of a future multi-TeV muon collider to charged LFV four-lepton interactions, establishing it as a powerful probe of the SMEFT parameter space.

hep-ph.title: Optimal Calibration-Free Observable for the Nucleon-Coupling Ratio in a Dual-Alkali Comagnetometer for Dark Matter Searches
hep-ph.author: Yossi Rosenzweig, Yevgeny Kats, Eli Sarid, Menachem Givon, Yonathan Japha, Ron Folman
hep-ph.abstract: A dual-alkali single-cell $^{87}$Rb-$^{39}$K-$^{3}$He comagnetometer can read an axion-like dark matter signal through two optical rotation channels, encoding the ratio $\mathcal{R}=\xi_n/\xi_p$ of the field's neutron and proton spin couplings in their relative response. The inter-species phase difference $\Delta\varphi$ has been proposed as a calibration-free readout that is sensitive to $\mathcal{R}$. Treating the extraction of $\mathcal{R}$ as a statistical estimation problem, we show that the estimate of $\mathcal{R}$ depends on the two channels only through their complex ratio, which splits into $\Delta\varphi$ and an amplitude ratio, of which only $\Delta\varphi$ is insensitive to the relative gain and hence calibration free. For our choice of comagnetometer parameters, above $\sim\!100$ Hz the phase difference alone captures most of the coupling-ratio information. At lower frequencies $\Delta\varphi$ is no longer near-sufficient. Below $\sim\!40$ Hz, the amplitude ratio would improve the precision on $\mathcal{R}$ by a factor of $\gtrsim2$. Recovering that information, however, requires the relative gain to be known sufficiently accurately, so $\Delta\varphi$ remains the robust observable even where it is not the most informative one.

hep-ph.title: Full-event anomaly detection for new physics searches at the Electron-Ion Collider
hep-ph.author: Dimitrios Athanasakos, Sebastian Grieninger, Hongkai Liu, Tymothy Mangan, Felix Ringer, Robert Szafron
hep-ph.abstract: The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will offer new opportunities to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study resonant anomaly detection using machine learning and the full particle content of an event. We consider a new neutral gauge boson and a heavy neutral lepton as illustrative signals with different electron-jet topologies. Weakly supervised learning uses this event information to enhance the sensitivity of an invariant-mass search without identifying individual signal events during training. Comparisons with high-level observables show that the electron kinematics account for an important part of the separation, while correlations among the particles provide further sensitivity. We also construct a conditional full-event generator by adapting a model pretrained on LHC jets to produce EIC background events. A scan over signal fractions demonstrates substantial signal enhancement using the learned background reference, providing a proof of concept for this approach at the EIC. Finally, we consider a fully unsupervised graph autoencoder that provides modest signal enhancement but retains sensitivity at signal fractions too small for effective weak supervision. Our results motivate full-event anomaly detection as part of the EIC physics program and identify directions for developing methods suited to its distinct kinematics.

hep-ph.title: A massive right-handed sterile neutrino in three-body ${\bar B}\to D^*\ell^-{\bar N}_R$ decays - a Monte Carlo simulation study
hep-ph.author: Bhubanjyoti Bhattacharya, Thomas E. Browder, Lucien M. Cremaldi, Horacio Crotte Ledesma, Nilakshi Das, Alakabha Datta, Tejhas Kapoor, Kumar Pandey, Alexei Sibidanov
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the differential decay distributions of $\bar{B}\to D^*\ell^-{\bar N}_R $, where $N_R$ is a heavy right-handed neutrino (RHN) and $\ell = e, \mu$. We employ a newly developed Monte Carlo event generator based on the EvtGen framework that can simulate beyond-the-Standard-Model processes. We validate the implementation of the model by comparing the Monte-Carlo results with analytical results for several kinematic variables such as $q^2$ and missing mass, as well as signatures in the angular distributions such as $A_{FB}$, $S_{3}$, $S_{5}$, etc. This MC Generator will enable new experimental searches for RHNs. We discuss the sensitivity of various observables to the presence of an RHN and the feasibility of an experimental analysis at Belle II.

hep-ph.title: Learning Astrophysical Uncertainties in Dark Matter Direct Detection with Simulation-Based Inference
hep-ph.author: Felix Kahlhoefer, Niklas Reus
hep-ph.abstract: We present a proof-of-concept study of neural ratio estimation (NRE) - a simulation-based inference algorithm - applied to WIMP direct detection using the XENONnT experiment as an example. A binary classifier is trained on simulated parameter-observation pairs to approximate the likelihood ratio for the WIMP mass $m_\chi$ and spin-independent proton coupling $c_p$, using realistic scintillation and ionization signals produced by the fuse detector simulation. We demonstrate that astrophysical uncertainties from halo model variations are marginalized over implicitly and at no additional inference cost by including multiple halo models in the training data. Using extreme $\pm5\sigma$ Standard Halo Model variations, we show that training on a combined dataset recovers well-calibrated posteriors even under severe misspecification, while more realistic halo models produce nearly indistinguishable results. The signal-plus-background classifier yields an exclusion limit that is both qualitatively and (after accounting for differences between frequentist and Bayesian approaches) quantitatively consistent with the XENONnT expected sensitivity. These results establish NRE as a scalable complement to the profile likelihood ratio approach, with particular advantages as experiments probe deeper into the neutrino fog.

hep-ph.title: Reassessing the Connection Between the Color Glass Condensate and TMD PDFs
hep-ph.author: Benjamin Guiot
hep-ph.abstract: Paying particular attention to the different types of gluons, collinear, soft and Glauber, we argue that, in its standard formulation, the CGC does not contain the collinear sector required for a meaningful comparison with TMD factorization. The CGC Wilson lines usually identified as part of the proton matrix element should instead be interpreted as the equivalent of a soft factor. Restoring the missing collinear exchanges, we obtain a new definition of small-$x$ PDFs from an explicit calculation of the DIS cross section using CGC Feynman rules. The resulting expression can be cast in a form resembling TMD factorization without being equivalent to it. Finally, we discuss the evolution of these small-$x$ PDFs with respect to the rapidity cutoff $\Lambda$ and the Bjorken variable $x_b$.

hep-ph.title: Stability of Vacuum and Quantum Dynamics in Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
hep-ph.author: Shi-Yuan Li, Chengwu Liu
hep-ph.abstract: Canonical quantization on scalar and Maxwell fields is studied for the stability of vacuum and construction of quantum dynamics in Anti-de Sitter spacetimes. The $\xi R\phi^2$ term in the Lagrangian of scalar field with $\xi > 5/48$ (mass term just introduces shift of $\xi$) can cause the spectrum of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian with negative value not bounded from below. The degrees of freedom corresponding to the negative values are constrained system and are ambiguous in space direction and in commutation relation. The only other algebra accommodated in 3-dimensional space consistent with locality, the anti-commutation relation, is definite confronting the constrain, and trivialize the negative spectrum to be inactive and absent degrees of freedom. Thus only the physical bosons corresponding to the non-negative spectrum span the Hilbert space. For the Maxwell fields as another constrained system, the gauge invariant canonical energy momentum tensor straightforwardly leads to the gauge invariant non-negative Hamiltonian. The 2-dimensional independent dynamical degrees of freedom are quantized in temporal gauge. The energy momentum tensors for both quantized fields are renormalized to be finite at operator level, which guarantee the stable vacuum maximally symmetric and the particle Fock states the representation of the AdS symmetry SO(2,3). Adopting Weinberg's framework, the new covariant free quantum scalar field is reconstructed in the corresponding mode function space isomorphic to the free boson Hilbert space, allowing various local effective interaction terms among fields introduced. The Yang-Feldman equations relate the free fields and the interacting fields with the Green functions determined properly in the mode function space.

hep-ph.title: Primordial Black Hole interpretation of the subsolar merger event S251112cm
hep-ph.author: Md Riajul Haque, Fabio Iocco, Luca Visinelli
hep-ph.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) candidate event S251112cm suggests that at least one component has a subsolar mass. Since such objects cannot be produced through standard stellar evolution, this observation provides a possible indication of nonstandard formation channels. Primordial black holes (PBHs), formed from the collapse of primordial density fluctuations in the early Universe, are a well-motivated candidate. We investigate the interpretation of S251112cm as the merger of two PBHs in the mass range $0.20$-$1\,M_\odot$, within the parameter space directly covered by the O4a subsolar search. Combining analytic estimates of the PBH merger rate with current observational constraints on their abundance and the sensitivity of LVK searches, we compute the probability of observing such an event. We consider both a monochromatic PBH mass function and extended lognormal distributions. Within the relaxed constraint scenario, the detection probability can approach unity toward the upper end of the mass range. A lognormal mass distribution of moderate width can enhance the probability relative to the monochromatic case, whereas a broader distribution can instead suppress it. Our results show that a PBH interpretation of S251112cm is compatible with current observational bounds even for a subdominant PBH abundance. Owing to the dependence of our results on astrophysical uncertainties, such as those affecting the constraints on the abundance of PBHs, they cannot be regarded as conclusive with respect to the nature of the detected event. At the same time, our analysis highlights the potential of subsolar gravitational wave events as a probe of PBHs and their contribution to dark matter.

hep-ph.title: Loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime: The parity-split IBP system and $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations
hep-ph.author: Jiaqi Chen, Bo Feng, Zhehan Qin, Yi-Xiao Tao
hep-ph.abstract: We develop integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals of cosmological correlators in de Sitter (dS) spacetime, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We identify a structural property of the dS IBP system: for an $n$-propagator family, it splits into $2^n$ closed subsystems classified by the parity of the propagator indices. We further formulate a Baikov representation for loop integrals in dS space and derive the corresponding dimensional recurrence relations. In flat spacetime, intersection theory shows that $\mathrm{d}\log$-form master integrands lead to $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations. Motivated by fibration intersection theory, we conjecture that this construction extends to dS integrands involving Hankel functions. We verify this conjecture in the one-loop bubble family and determine the associated alphabet.

hep-ph.title: Hybrid neutron stars among mass gap objects are excluded by twin stars at $1.4\,M_\odot$
hep-ph.author: Alexander Ayriyan, David Blaschke, Marcin Dubaj, Oleksandr Vitiuk, Adrian Wojcik
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the question whether compact objects in the so-called mass gap ($2.5 < M/M_\odot < 5.0$) can be neutron stars or hybrid stars. Using a generic hybrid star equation of state with a first-order deconfinement transition, we map the allowed parameter space in a Seidov-type diagram and confront it with modern mass-radius constraints. We find that mass-gap hybrid stars require an extremely early onset of deconfinement and very stiff quark matter. The Bayesian analysis, however, favors equations of state with deconfinement at typical neutron-star masses around $1.4\,M_\odot$ with mass-twin stars that, if confirmed, would rule out hybrid stars as candidates for observed mass-gap compact objects.

hep-ph.title: Reconstructing Early Primordial Black Hole Domination from Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds
hep-ph.author: Daniel del-Corral, Angus Spalding
hep-ph.abstract: Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) with masses below $\mathcal{O}(10^9)$g occupy an interesting region of parameter space that is largely inaccessible to conventional observations. Despite evaporating before Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), these PBHs can naturally generate a period of early matter domination in the early Universe. A primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) provides a window onto this otherwise inaccessible regime, since the modified expansion history leaves a characteristic spectral feature associated with the onset and end of PBH domination. The locations of these characteristic frequencies can be used to reconstruct the underlying PBH parameters, in particular the PBH mass. For a freely propagating GWB, the location of these frequencies additionally allow the initial PBH abundance to be determined. We derive simple numerical relations that map these characteristic frequencies directly onto the PBH mass and initial abundance. Future GW experiments span a vast frequency range, providing sensitivity to PBH masses from the BBN bound of $\mathcal{O}(10^9)\,\mathrm{g}$ down to the lower bound of $\mathcal{O}(10)\,\mathrm{g}$. We find that the nanohertz signal reported by NANOGrav, if primordial in origin, is already probing PBH masses in the range $4$--$90\,\mathrm{Mg}$. GW observations therefore offer access to a vast region of PBH parameter space that is otherwise beyond the reach of current experiments.

hep-ph.title: Absence of Continuous Spin Particles in Superstring Theory
hep-ph.author: Arwa Alabbasi(1), Fernando Quevedo(1 and 2) ((1) Department of Physics, New York University Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, (2) DAMTP, University of Cambridge, Wilberforce Road, Cambridge, UK)
hep-ph.abstract: The study of continuous spin particles, as general low-energy implications of relativity and quantum mechanics, has intensified in recent years with potential experimental signatures. In this note we show that these particles are absent in perturbative super-string theories, generalising a result inarXiv:1302.4771to the supersymmetric case. This stands out as a general low-energy prediction of all perturbative superstring constructions.

hep-lat.title: Evidence of Taste-Symmetry restoration for Kähler-Dirac fermions on Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations
hep-lat.author: Mingwei Dai, Walter Freeman, Mason Grieb, Jack Laiho, Marc Schiffer, Judah Unmuth-Yockey
hep-lat.abstract: We study the spectrum of two-particle bound states of Kähler-Dirac fermions coupled via gravity in Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations (EDT). We work in the quenched approximation, where the geometry is allowed to fluctuate, but there is no back-reaction from the matter on the geometry. The Kähler-Dirac action respects an exact $U(1)$ symmetry that is related to continuum chiral symmetry, and this $U(1)$ symmetry ensures that some of the bound-state masses vanish in the chiral limit of vanishing fermion bare mass. The bound-state masses that are not protected by the $U(1)$ symmetry do not vanish in the chiral limit, but the scale associated with the symmetry breaking does not appear to be a physical scale like the Planck mass or the curvature scale of the emergent de Sitter background. Rather, the mass scale associated with this non-degeneracy appears to be a positive power of the lattice spacing, decreasing as the continuum limit is approached. This suggests that Kähler-Dirac fermions in EDT can be interpreted as the gravity analog of staggered fermions in flat-space lattice field theories, with similar behavior.

hep-lat.title: Lattice Monte Carlo of $λϕ^4$ on Euclidean de Sitter
hep-lat.author: Angelo Caravano
hep-lat.abstract: We report the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space, $S^4$. Rather than discretizing space, we use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. For a massless $\lambda\phi^4$ theory, the zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, and deviations closely follow the one-loop renormalization of $\lambda$. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow. This saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. Our results confirm nonperturbatively that the infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism. More broadly, this work opens up de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.

hep-lat.title: Stochastic Path Sampler For Lattice Field Theory
hep-lat.author: Shiyang Chen, Moxian Qian, Gert Aarts, Biagio Lucini, Kai Zhou
hep-lat.abstract: In lattice field theory, target distributions are known only up to normalization, (\tilde{\pi}(\phi)\propto e^{-S(\phi)}), while the partition function is intractable. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations often become inefficient near phase transitions or the continuum limit due to critical slowing down. In this work, we propose a novel sampler based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, called Stochastic Path Sampler (SPS), which can generate configurations for the unnormalized target distribution without requiring training data. The central idea of SPS is to establish a trajectory-level balance for learnable forward and backward stochastic dynamics between two equilibrium states, namely the prior and target distributions. This is achieved by minimizing the path-space variational free energy, equivalently an entropy-production upper bound, defined by the log-ratio of forward and auxiliary backward trajectory measures, thereby enhancing the reversibility of the forward and backward processes. The learned forward process provides independent proposals, which are subsequently corrected by an extended-space Independence Metropolis--Hastings step. In two-dimensional (\phi^4) theory, we demonstrate that our neural sampler can achieve the same sampling quality as HMC but with a much shorter autocorrelation time in the critical region. This sampler offers a stochastic-quantization-inspired route to data-free proposal construction for lattice field theory by leveraging a variational free-energy principle derived from path-space irreversibility.

hep-lat.title: Looking for WIMPs through the neutrino fogs
hep-lat.author: Itay M. Bloch, Salvatore Bottaro, Diego Redigolo, Ludovico Vittorio
hep-lat.abstract: We revisit the expected sensitivity of large-scale xenon detectors to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). Assuming current primary noise sources can be mitigated, we find that with the present discrimination power between nuclear and electron recoils, the experimental sensitivity is limited not only by atmospheric neutrinos' nuclear recoils (''nuclear recoil neutrino fog'') but also by solar neutrinos' electron-recoil events (''electron recoil neutrino fog''). While this is known by experimentalists, it is often missed or misunderstood by theorists, and we therefore emphasize this effect. We set up a realistic detector simulation to quantify the contamination of the WIMP signal from both these neutrino backgrounds. We observe that the electron-recoil background remains significant even for signal rates exceeding those of atmospheric neutrinos, as predicted by most electroweak WIMP candidates. We update the projections for the required exposure to exclude/discover a given electroweak WIMP, streamlining the computation of their signal rates and uncertainties. We show that all of the real WIMPs with zero hypercharge can be excluded (discovered) with a 50 tonne year (300 tonne year) exposure. A similar exposure will allow to probe a large portion of the viable parameter space for complex WIMP with non-zero hypercharge.

hep-th.title: Lattice Monte Carlo of $λϕ^4$ on Euclidean de Sitter
hep-th.author: Angelo Caravano
hep-th.abstract: We report the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space, $S^4$. Rather than discretizing space, we use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. For a massless $\lambda\phi^4$ theory, the zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, and deviations closely follow the one-loop renormalization of $\lambda$. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow. This saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. Our results confirm nonperturbatively that the infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism. More broadly, this work opens up de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.

hep-th.title: Proving the OSV conjecture with the gravitational path integral
hep-th.author: Nikolay Bobev, Jan Boruch, Luca V. Iliesiu, Dawid Maskalaniec
hep-th.abstract: The OSV conjecture relates the helicity supertrace of black holes in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity obtained through a Calabi--Yau compactification of Type IIA string theory to the modulus squared of the topological string partition function evaluated at the attractor point in moduli space for a given set of magnetic black hole charges and electric chemical potentials. We find Euclidean black hole saddles that compute this index to all orders in the 4d supergravity derivative expansion and calculate their action using equivariant localization. The gravitational on-shell action localizes entirely to the north and south poles of each black hole, with the two contributions determined by the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic topological string free energies, respectively, evaluated at the attractor values of the moduli. For single-center black hole saddles, this provides a proof of the OSV conjecture to all orders in the topological string coupling. The same localization formula also applies to all saddles that contribute to the helicity supertrace, such as multi-center black holes, which leads to a non-perturbative refinement of the conjecture.

hep-th.title: GLSMs for non-polynomial deformations and generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds
hep-th.author: Lara B. Anderson, James Gray, Eric Sharpe, Albert Haochen Zhang
hep-th.abstract: Gauged Linear Sigma Models (GLSMs) have long been a key tool in understanding Calabi-Yau compactifications of string theory. While descriptions of complete intersections of polynomial defining equations have long been understood in this context, a full treatment of non-polynomial complex structure deformations has been absent from the literature. Likewise, the somewhat more exotic generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau construction has resisted a GLSM description. In this paper we resolve both of these omissions using completely standard GLSMs with polynomial superpotentials. The non-polynomial structure seen in the geometric constructions only arises in the associated GLSM upon restriction to the vacuum space of the theory. This feature enables the construction to avoid singularities in field space that could have arisen if non-polynomial structure were incorporated directly into the GLSM superpotential.

hep-th.title: Quantum limit to transparency
hep-th.author: Angelo Esposito, Alberto Nicolis, Federico Piazza
hep-th.abstract: We argue that no material can be made completely transparent to light as long as it has a nontrivial index of refraction. The quantum decay of photons into phonons is an ineliminable source of attenuation. This survives even once all other excitations have been gapped away, impurities have been removed, and the temperature has been set to zero. Restricting for simplicity to the case of a superfluid, we determine via effective field theory methods the corresponding low-frequency contribution to the imaginary part of the index of refraction. This scales as $\omega^4$ and induces a nonanalyticity of the real part for $\omega \rightarrow 0$. We also extend our result to large coherent electromagnetic fields, such as those of a laser, showing that the effect can receive strong nonlinear enhancements. Our result is a genuine quantum lower bound to the transparency of a medium.

hep-th.title: The Real EFThedron: A Moment Geometry for the Nonperturbative S-Matrix
hep-th.author: Laurentiu Rodina, Anna Tokareva, Yongjun Xu
hep-th.abstract: The S-matrix bootstrap restricts low-energy interactions through unitarity, analyticity and crossing symmetry. For effective field theory couplings, positivity bounds have a natural geometric formulation, the EFThedron, in which the allowed couplings form the classical positive moment problem. We show that this geometry extends to full nonlinear unitarity. Multiplying the amplitude by fractional powers of the energy turns its real part into a moment as well, so that unitarity becomes a bounded complex moment problem. Analyticity becomes a set of linear constraints requiring different kernels to reconstruct the same couplings, analogous to the null constraints imposed by crossing symmetry. In two dimensions the problem can be solved exactly, leading to Castillejo--Dalitz--Dyson amplitudes as extremal measures of the moment problem. In four dimensions we obtain closed-form and semi-analytic bounds for the massless EFThedron model and for massive scalar scattering. For massive scalars, the analyticity constraints improve on published dual bounds, reducing the gap to the primal region. By placing the real and imaginary parts of amplitudes on an equal footing, the Real EFThedron provides a powerful framework combining unitarity, analyticity and crossing, opening a new route to mapping the space of consistent quantum field theories.

hep-th.title: Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
hep-th.author: Michael Borinsky, Jury Radkovski, Suriyah Rajalingam Kannagi
hep-th.abstract: A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in $D=2$ and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the $\beta$-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.

hep-th.title: Could four-dimensional $ϕ^4$ theory exist beyond the usual triviality arguments?
hep-th.author: Anton Ragin(Imperial College London)
hep-th.abstract: Do lattice triviality, suspected Borel non-summability and the perturbative Landau pole exclude an interacting four-dimensional theory satisfying the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms and reproducing every renormalized coefficient of positive-coupling $O(N)$ $\phi^4$ theory? An example involving one real function separates vanishing cutoff limits along its allowed bare trajectories from a nonzero result obtained by renormalizing the coefficients first; an exponentially small correction preserves its expansion and removes the pole in its running coupling. For the massless two-point expansion of the singlet composite $\Phi_a\Phi_a$ at leading order in $1/N$, ordinary Borel summation fails even for Gaussian smearing. The arithmetic mean of two Borel integrals along opposite imaginary rays defines a real distribution on every four-dimensional Schwartz momentum or position test, with finite-order remainder bounds uniform on bounded test sets. Two alternative covariances with nonnegative mass spectral weights remove the Euclidean pole and construct generalized free fields. After a fixed contact subtraction, their Euclidean extensions preserve every coefficient of the collective correlations obtained by Wick pairing. The interacting finite-$N$ family remains open. We also state a conditional interacting route through the physical scalar correlations of a larger theory (the parent) with heavy particles. A concrete $N=1$ gauge--Higgs--fermion candidate has a tuned one-loop trajectory on which all interaction couplings tend to zero in the ultraviolet, and a stable tree vacuum with additional masses comparable to the heavy scale. Constructing the parent and its corrected ultraviolet trajectory, and proving coefficient decoupling and the exact remainder bounds as the quartic coupling tends to zero and the family's heavy masses grow, remain open.

hep-th.title: Brane space localization and genus-0 T-duality with $H$-flux
hep-th.author: Fei Han(NUS), Varghese Mathai(Adelaide U.)
hep-th.abstract: We construct a geometric theory on the brane space $S^2M=C^\infty(S^2,M)$ associated to a gerbe with connection on $M$. Normalized logarithmic holonomy around the latitude circles defines an average holonomy line bundle on the brane space, whose connection and averaged flux give an equivariantly flat superconnection. We prove that the completed periodic exotic twisted cohomology defined by this superconnection localizes to the twisted cohomology of $M$. This {\bf brane space localization} happens in two stages: circle localization lands on the free path space of $M$, and contracting the paths, after a correction of the twisting form, brings us back to $M$.Parallel transport along the meridians lets us average gerbe module connections, after which the circular iterated-integral construction applies. The resulting {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern forms} restrict to the twisted Chern forms on $M$; their variation is described by {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern-Simons forms.}For a T-dual pair, transporting the classical Hori morphisms through localization yields {\bf graded genus-0 T-duality} on brane cohomology. The composite of each morphism with its dual is minus the Euler operator in the level variable, so these morphisms are isomorphisms at every nonzero level. At level one these morphisms are compatible with the brane character and twisted $K$-theory T-duality.

hep-th.title: Distinguishing Flat and Warped Extra Dimensions with Unruh-DeWitt Detectors
hep-th.author: Ashmita Das, Anjana Krishnan, Soumitra Sengupta
hep-th.abstract: We examine the response of a two level Unruh-DeWitt (UD) detector interacting with the Kaluza-Klein (KK) mass modes of a bulk scalar field in extra dimensional models. Considering two of the promising extra dimensional models with distinct compactifications, such as large, flat extra dimensions in the Arkani Hamed, Dimopoulos \& Dvali (ADD) framework and warped extra dimensions in the Randall-Sundrum (RS) scenario, we compute the profile function of the detector. We extend this computation to the 6 dimensional doubly compactified spacetime geometry. The profile function of the detector has been examined as a function of the energy gap of the detector, the compactification radius of the extra dimension, and the dimensionality of spacetime, requiring the chosen parameter space appropriately such that the gauge hierarchy problem is duly addressed. We find that the pattern of the profile function is dictated by the spacing of the KK mass spectrum and the resolution of the detector. For ADD model, the spacing between successive KK modes decreases with the increasing compactification radius, yielding a smoothly increasing continuum pattern in the profile function. Whereas for the RS warped geometry model, a tiny deviation in the radius of the extra dimension produces a large change in the same, resulting a sharp increment. The resolvability of the KK mode structure is sensitive to the underlying geometry of the spacetime, providing a qualitative distinction between flat and warped extra dimensional scenarios within the UD detector framework.

hep-th.title: Disformal Closure Selects 3D Scalar-Tensor Gravity without Local Bulk Modes
hep-th.author: M. Shams Nejati, M.H. Vahidinia
hep-th.abstract: Three-dimensional Einstein gravity has no local degrees of freedom, yet retains rich global and black-hole physics. Adding a scalar normally spoils this. We show that closure of three-dimensional Horndeski gravity under disformal field redefinitions selects a square-root curvature interaction. A nonlinear analysis finds no local bulk modes on regular branches, while an independent Hamiltonian analysis confirms the result on the timelike-gradient branch. This extends the no-local-bulk-dynamics paradigm beyond pure Einstein gravity and motivates studying its boundary and global sectors.

hep-th.title: Dirac-Born-Infeld action from inequivalent representations of open strings
hep-th.author: Isao Kishimoto, Tomohiko Takahashi, Ayane Tezuka
hep-th.abstract: We study open strings in a constant magnetic field from the viewpoint of universal canonical variables. Using a conserved Klein-Gordon-type pairing, we show that the canonical commutation relations remain background independent in the distributional sense, while the background dependence is encoded in the mode representation. The Bogoliubov transformation between different magnetic backgrounds is not unitarily implementable, so that the corresponding Fock representations are inequivalent. Nevertheless, the transformation determines the relative normalization of the vacua. We show that the resulting relative vacuum normalization precisely reproduces the relative boundary $g$-function, or equivalently the magnetic-field-dependent part of the disk amplitude, and yields the Dirac-Born-Infeld factor. Thus the disk normalization is encoded directly in the transformation between inequivalent representations of universal open-string variables.

hep-th.title: The origin of amplitude chaos and strings
hep-th.author: Pallab Basu, Anurag Sarkar
hep-th.abstract: We analytically study the peak statistics of an amplitude ensemble to identify the local mechanism responsible for peak repulsion. Our analytical approaches show that a smooth, nondegenerate ensemble of sufficiently differentiable amplitudes exhibits quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion, $p_{\rm nn}(S)\sim S^4$, where $S$ is the spacing between adjacent peaks. We verify this prediction numerically for the tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes. Interestingly, we find the quartic repulsion to be robust by varying both the underlying ensemble and the amplitude functions, whereas a tunable cusp model shows that weakening differentiability changes the strength of the repulsion. Peak repulsion therefore defines a local universality class that is not unique to string theory and may occur in amplitude ensembles in other theories.

hep-th.title: The Casimir energy in Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics with various perfect electric or magnetic boundary condition combinations
hep-th.author: Philipe De Fabritiis, Wellisson B. De Lima, David Dudal
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the Casimir effect between two parallel wires in $(2+1)D$ Maxwell-Chern-Simons (MCS) electrodynamics under different boundary conditions and separated by a distance $L$. Using a functional approach in which the boundary constraints are implemented by auxiliary fields localized on the wires, we integrate out the gauge field and derive an effective boundary theory whose functional determinant allows us to compute the Casimir energy. We consider perfect electric conductor (PEC), perfect magnetic conductor (PMC), and infinitely permeable (PMC2) boundary conditions. For two PEC wires, we recover the known MCS result and show that it coincides with the result obtained in the Abelian limit of the Curci-Ferrari (CF) model, implying that the Casimir effect in this case probes the photon mass $\mu$ but not its origin. The same energy is obtained for two PMC2 wires. In sharp contrast, the Casimir energy vanishes identically for the covariant PMC condition in MCS theory, both for PMC-PMC and PEC-PMC. Since this cancellation does not occur in the CF model, it could provide a signature of the topological origin of the photon mass in $(2+1)D$. Finally, the PEC-PMC2 case yields a non-vanishing Casimir force and reproduces the known result for a perfectly conducting wire facing an infinitely permeable one. Interestingly enough, we show that for PEC-PMC2, the Casimir force in the MCS theory is smaller than the one of the CF model for any $L,\mu >0$. Our results thus show that, depending on the boundary conditions, the Casimir effect could probe not only the photon mass but also reveal signatures of its origin.

hep-th.title: Confining Random Potential Quantum Mechanics for Jackiw-Teitelboim Gravity
hep-th.author: Dongsu Bak, Chanju Kim, Sang-Heon Yi
hep-th.abstract: We formulate perturbative Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity as an ensemble of ordinary one-dimensional Hamiltonians with a confining random potential. The leading profile reproduces the disk density of states, while connected cumulants of a single master field encode the topological expansion. After formulating the cumulant power counting required by the topological expansion, we show that the cumulants reproduce all genus-zero multi-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{0,n}$. At higher genus, we show that a renormalization scheme can be chosen consistently order by order so that imposing one-boundary polynomiality recursively reproduces the perturbative JT string equation and yields the standard JT one-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{g,1}$. The framework provides a self-contained finite-$S_0$ quantum dynamics with a discrete spectrum and unitary real time evolution, beyond a mere rewriting of the matrix integral. The same confining dynamics also underlies late-time saturation and the dynamical avoidance of the would-be black hole singularity, as shown in our earlier work.

hep-th.title: Codimension-Zero Holographic Complexity and Spectral Three-Point Correlators
hep-th.author: Masamichi Miyaji, Shan-Ming Ruan, Shono Shibuya, Kazuyoshi Yano
hep-th.abstract: Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections ultimately leading to a late-time saturation. We develop a spectral formulation of holographic complexity measures associated with codimension-zero bulk regions in the framework of the complexity=anything proposal. The corresponding generating function of complexity is governed by three-point correlation functions of the density of states, establishing a direct connection between bulk geometric observables and nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. We find that the codimension-zero holographic complexity reduces to the sum of two codimension-one contributions and exhibits a universal time evolution, characterized by an exponentially long regime of linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time. The late-time plateau is a direct result of the spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems, thereby providing a universal mechanism for the saturation of holographic complexity. We also develop a complementary operator interpretation, in which Euclidean wormhole corrections render the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete. Constructing a complete orthonormal basis then yields well-defined holographic complexity operators that reproduce the same universal time evolution. Our results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity.

hep-th.title: General relativity and its modifications as effective field theories of $GL(4)$ breaking
hep-th.author: Tommaso Viacava, Omar Zanusso
hep-th.abstract: We discuss General Relativity and some of its modifications as effective field theories of the breaking of the affine general linear group using the coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form. While the ultimate goal is to break the symmetry down to the Lorentz subgroup, we argue that there are three interesting breaking cascades in which the affine general linear group is first broken to a larger subgroup that contains the Lorentz group. In all cases, the breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes that can be interpreted as metric degrees of freedom. We argue that the effective field theories that emerge as a result of the different breaking patterns are all dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion, e.g., using Einstein-Hilbert-like actions, but can differ beyond the leading order.

hep-th.title: On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian
hep-th.author: José Luis V. Cerdeira, Tomás Ortín
hep-th.abstract: We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

hep-th.title: Dualities, symmetries and the elliptic genus of 2d (0,2) SCFTs
hep-th.author: Salomon Malka, Gabi Zafrir
hep-th.abstract: While naively simpler than its higher dimensional cousins, 2d physics still has its own share of puzzles. An example of this is instances of dualities of $(0,2)$ theories, passing all consistency checks save for a mismatch in global symmetry. This is common when said duality can be motivated by dimensional reduction of a duality of 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories where said symmetry emerges in 2d, often from an anomalous 4d symmetry. It is commonly believed that these symmetries are broken in the 2d theory, though often the mechanism for such breaking is not understood. We examine various appearances of this phenomenon and show that in these cases the elliptic genus shows signs of the presence of marginal operators that can break these symmetries. Interestingly, these operators do not appear perturbatively but emerge from the calculation, raising the question of what operators the $(0,2)$ elliptic genus actually counts. This provides a potential mechanism to overcome the discrepancy in symmetry, though we point out some potential subtleties.

hep-th.title: Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations
hep-th.author: Nicola Baglioni, Daniele Bielli, Parita Shah, Gabriele Tartaglino-Mazzucchelli
hep-th.abstract: We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $\nu$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described by a reduced gravitational potential. We show that the resulting framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation of its equations of motion on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Finally, within the Lorentz-invariant family and the zweibein deformations of conformal matter theories considered here, we identify $T\bar{T}$ as the only deformation that can be interpreted as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.

hep-th.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
hep-th.author: Jasper Nongmaithem, Deepak Kumar Kar, Ayush Kumar, Shreeya Rajesh Parab, David Dudal, Subhash Mahapatra
hep-th.abstract: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

hep-th.title: Robustness of exact $SU(N)$ Einstein-Skyrme solutions: black holes, wormholes and cosmologies
hep-th.author: Carla Henríquez-Baez, Perla Medina, Pablo Rodríguez, Aldo Vera
hep-th.abstract: The $SU(2)$ Skyrme model admits exact solutions when coupled to General Relativity in four spacetime dimensions. Here, we demonstrate that relevant gravitational configurations, such as black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies, are robust under the extension to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors. We show that key physical features, such as the thermodynamic properties, the baryon number of the configurations, and the geometry, are crucially determined by the number of flavors as well as the coupling constants of the theory. In particular: first, we prove that an increase in the matter content favors the local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes. Second, for cosmological solutions, we demonstrate analytically that as the hadronic matter content increases, the scale factor grows more slowly due to enhanced gravitational attraction, while the expansion rate (measured by the Hubble parameter) increases as a consequence of the higher energy density. Third, we find that the throat of traversable wormhole solutions can be enlarged by increasing the number of flavors, since the energy density required to keep the throat open does not grow indefinitely but rather saturates at a finite value.

hep-th.title: Dynamical symmetry breaking in a non-polynomial four-fermion model
hep-th.author: J. F. Assunção, T. Mariz, A. Yu. Petrov, V. Prata
hep-th.abstract: We present a new four-fermion model with a strongly non-polynomial coupling. To eliminate these non-polynomialities, we introduce two auxiliary vector fields and show that the dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking is possible in our theory, as revealed by the effective potential generated for these vector fields. We explicitly calculate the low-energy effective action for these fields, which is given by the sum of three Maxwell terms (one for each field and a mixed one) plus a potential term displaying nontrivial minima.

hep-th.title: G2 resolutions and backtracking in scale-separated AdS$_3$
hep-th.author: Aviral Aggarwal, Fien Apers, Fotis Farakos
hep-th.abstract: We study scale-separated AdS$_3$ models with full moduli stabilization in massive IIA supergravity on G2 orientifolds. In addition to constructing new examples, we investigate the properties of these models once the singularities of the G2 toroidal orbifold are resolved. The blow-up moduli are shown to be stabilized using fluxes in a parametric regime that preserves scale separation and control under the supergravity approximation. We further show that the apparent orientifold intersections in the singular orbifold description do not exist on such resolved spaces. Finally, we analyze the brane dual picture of such models using flux backtracking. We highlight several interesting features from such analysis such as a finite interval solution of the resulting flow equations in some of the models and the desirable low-energy decoupling of brane modes.

hep-th.title: The Gregory-Laflamme Instability of five-dimensional Black Strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
hep-th.author: Pau Figueras, Áron D. Kovács, Shunhui Yao
hep-th.abstract: We complement and extend our recent study of the non-linear evolution of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions. First, we study time-dependent perturbations of uniform black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory and determine the growth rates as a function of the coupling. We find that for positive Gauss-Bonnet couplings, the black strings are more unstable than in general relativity in the sense that the growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. In the second part of the paper we show that the hyperbolicity of the equation of motion of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory is determined by an effective metric when the dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in the asymptotically flat directions. When the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as it happens near the endpoint of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of the black string, this effective metric becomes degenerate and the Cauchy evolution breaks down. Applying this criterion to uniform black strings, we find that for any positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the one of minimal thickness) on which the effective metric degenerates in a neighbourhood of the horizon. Therefore, we argue that these solutions cannot be attained from weakly coupled initial data by Cauchy evolution and the solutions of the linearized equations around them cannot be interpreted as approximations to nearby non-linear evolutions. We provide further evidence for this picture with non-linear simulations of the Gregory-Laflamme instability. The non-linear simulations terminate through a loss of hyperbolicity of the Tricomi or Keldysh type, depending on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling.

hep-th.title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
hep-th.author: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar
hep-th.abstract: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $\kappa$-class dressing.

hep-th.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
hep-th.author: Ashis Tamang, Nishal Rai, Javier Esteban, Eugenio Megias
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ and $\Delta=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

hep-th.title: The Quasiparticle Ansatz for Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product States
hep-th.author: Silviu S. Pufu, Benjamin T. Søgaard, Spyros Terlemes
hep-th.abstract: The Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product State (RCMPS) ansatz introduced inarXiv:2102.07741is a translation-invariant variational ansatz intended to approximate the ground states of gapped one-dimensional relativistic Quantum Field Theories directly in the continuum limit and in infinite volume. In this work, we develop an ansatz, referred to as the Relativistic Quasiparticle (RQP) ansatz, for the low-lying one-particle excitations of the RCMPS vacuum, as well as for solitons interpolating between two distinct degenerate vacua. The corresponding energies of these states can be obtained as the eigenvalues of an effective Hamiltonian. The RQP ansatz generalizes constructions used in the Matrix Product State and Continuous Matrix Product State literature. We apply the RQP ansatz to the sine-Gordon model and find good agreement with results from integrability for both the soliton and breather masses. We also apply the RQP ansatz to the $\phi^4$ theory, in both its $\mathbb Z_2$-preserving and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-broken phases, and determine the spectrum of particles and solitons. This enables us to determine the parameter regime for which multiple stable particles exist.

hep-th.title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
hep-th.author: Faisal Karimi
hep-th.abstract: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$\sigma$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $\alpha_\sigma$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

hep-th.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
hep-th.author: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat
hep-th.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

hep-th.title: Reflected entropy and islands in JT gravity from partial dimensional reduction
hep-th.author: Debarshi Basu, Himanshu Chourasiya
hep-th.abstract: We study how mixed-state correlations reorganize across island transitions in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to a non-gravitating bath. Using the partial-dimensional-reduction realization of double holography, we compute reflected entropy for adjacent and disjoint radiation regions in the vacuum and in the thermofield-double state of an eternal black hole.
