Reflected entropy probes the internal partition of the entanglement wedge and therefore resolves structure that is invisible to the ordinary Page curve: its dominant saddle can change even when the entropy saddle of the union remains fixed, and it vanishes at leading order when the entanglement wedge disconnects. We show that the lower-dimensional reflected-island description agrees, to leading order in the dynamical brane fluctuation, with the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface picture. The finite-angle comparison further suggests a projection-covariant identification of island and brane endpoints at linear order. The resulting Page-like curves and Markov gaps provide a geometric probe of the reorganization of the purification and of non-Markovian, multipartite correlation structure during island transitions.

hep-th.title: A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra
hep-th.author: Ritabrata Bhattacharya, Abhay Katyal, Oscar Varela
hep-th.abstract: We determine a universal sector of the spectrum of light operators in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ superconformal field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a compact hyperbolic Riemann surface $\Sigma_2$. We work at large $N$, analysing Kaluza--Klein fluctuations about the dual Bah--Beem--Bobev--Wecht anti-de Sitter backgrounds for general values of the twist parameter $z$. To obtain these spectra, we specialise recently derived mass operators to modes that are constant on $\Sigma_2$ by imposing a suitable $z$-dependent generalised $G$-structure. We then organise the resulting eigenstates into long and protected $\mathcal{N}=1$ supermultiplets with definite flavour quantum numbers. As $z$ varies, rich patterns emerge in the spectrum, including both isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, which we characterise analytically.

hep-th.title: Effective field theory for strong phase transitions
hep-th.author: Oliver Gould, Farbod-Sayyed Rassouli, Paul M. Saffin
hep-th.abstract: We show how to construct perturbative effective field theories for strong phase transitions, where the standard tools of high-temperature dimensional reduction fail. By identifying the relevant power counting relations for the couplings, masses and background fields, we construct a controlled perturbative expansion adapted to this regime. We find that the order parameter field remains light at the transition, so that there is a controlled derivative expansion, even though large external fields need to be resummed. The resulting effective field theories for strong phase transitions live in three dimensions and have nonpolynomial field dependence. Applying our framework to a two-scalar model, we verify renormalisation scale cancellation through next-to-next-to-leading order and find decreasing corrections to the latent heat as the perturbative order is increased. Extending to include fermions and gauge fields, we identify a broad class of models in which strong-transition thermodynamics are systematically improvable.

hep-th.title: Multipartite entanglement spreads
hep-th.author: Sylvain Carrozza, Johann Chevrier, Luca Lionni
hep-th.abstract: The entanglement structure of a bipartite pure state is characterized by its entanglement spectrum, or equivalently, by the family of Rényi-$k$ entanglement entropies with integer $k$. Taking the difference of two such entropies defines a quantity known as an entanglement spread, that is monotonous under local operations, and that vanishes if and only if the entanglement spectrum of the state is flat. We introduce a multipartite generalization of this notion which, for a fixed number $D\geq 3$ of parties, results in a collection of maps indexed by pairs of $D$-edge-colored graphs (obeying some condition). Each member of this collection takes the form of a difference of two multipartite Rényi entanglement entropies, each associated to a local unitary polynomial invariant (known in this context as a trace-invariant), and is shown to be monotonous under local operations. We then argue that a previously introduced family of so-called hypergraph-tensor (HT) states can be understood as a multipartite counterpart to the family of flat bipartite states. Indeed, we first prove that, when $D=3$, a tripartite pure state is HT if and only if it minimizes a particular (infinite) family of entanglement spreads. Second, we embed the set of HT states into the much larger family of spectral hypergraph-tensor (SHT) states, defined by a new Ansatz we introduce. We then prove that HT states can be uniquely characterized as the minimizers of some fixed entanglement spread among SHT states, for arbitrary $D\geq 3$. We also investigate SHT states in their own right: in particular, we characterize their orbits under local unitary transformations. Finally, along the way, the asymptotic large-$N$ expectation values of a number of entanglement spreads are computed in the Haar-random state of local dimension $N$.

hep-th.title: Asymptotic AEther Misalignment and Universal-Horizon Mechanics
hep-th.author: Walter Arata, Moustafa Ismail, Stefano Liberati, David Mattingly, Luke Martin, Giulio Neri
hep-th.abstract: Universal horizons trap even arbitrarily fast signals, providing a test of black-hole thermodynamics in theories with a preferred time direction. In Einstein--aether theory, this direction is defined by a dynamical field, the aether, that can remain non-aligned relative to stationary time at infinity. In particular, for asymptotically anti-de Sitter black holes, it was so far impossible to recover a first law of black-hole mechanics when such asymptotic tilt of the aether is present. Here, we resolve this issue for an exact family of static, spherically symmetric solutions. Using the covariant phase-space formalism, we identify the asymptotic tilt and the decaying part of the aether field as a boundary source and its conjugate response. Allowing both to vary independently obstructs the definition of an energy that generates time translations. Fixing either quantity, or imposing a relation between them, restores such an energy, while externally varying the boundary data introduces work into the first law. The energies obtained by fixing the source or its response are related by a Legendre transformation. At the universal horizon, heat includes both the metric area contribution and an irreducible aether energy flux. The resulting balance separates work at infinity from horizon heat and explains why the physical temperature cannot generally be inferred from the coefficient of an area variation in the black-hole mass.

hep-th.title: Dissipative Majorana Chain---Anomalies and Non-Invertible Symmetries
hep-th.author: Hung-Hsuan Teh, Tokiro Numasawa
hep-th.abstract: We study symmetries and anomalies of dissipative Majorana chains described by Lindblad dynamics. Using the operator-state mapping, we represent the Lindbladian as a non-Hermitian operator on a doubled Hilbert space. In this formulation, the ket and bra contours admit strong fermion parities and strong translations, while their diagonal combinations define weak symmetries. For even and odd chain lengths, we diagnose anomalies by comparing symmetry algebras with and without weak fermion-parity defects. These algebras retain the lattice precursor of the modulo-$8$ anomaly of the closed Majorana chain and exhibit projective relations between strong fermion parity and weak translation, as well as between weak fermion parity and strong translation, which are intrinsic to open quantum systems. We establish the IR correspondence between the lattice symmetry algebras and those of the doubled Majorana CFT in four spin sectors, identifying chiral fermion parities emanated from the lattice translations. Finally, we develop the lattice bosonization of the dissipative chain. For even length with collective energy dephasing, combining the defect and no-defect sectors and imposing GSO projections gives rise to an Ising Lindbladian with non-invertible Kramers--Wannier symmetries descending from the anomalous strong translation and fermion parity of the Majorana chain. For odd length, constructing mutually commuting ket- and bra-sector spin operators instead yields an Ising Lindbladian with a Kramers--Wannier duality defect. Our results provide a controlled framework for extending lattice anomalies and non-invertible symmetries to open quantum systems.

hep-th.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
hep-th.author: Abdias Aires, Tatsuya Daniel
hep-th.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

hep-th.title: Quantum geometric inflation
hep-th.author: Nephtalí Eliceo Martínez Pérez, Cupatitzio Ramírez Romero
hep-th.abstract: Geometric Inflation adds an infinite tower of curvature invariants to the Einstein-Hilbert action while preserving certain key features such as leading to second order modified Friedmann equations for FRW backgrounds. Sourcing them with a perfect barotropic fluid can easily produce a slow-roll inflationary regime, no inflaton field is required. In this work, we perform the Wheeler-DeWitt quantization of minisuperspace Geometric Inflation models. First, we construct an effective 1D FRW action and perform the Hamiltonian formulation using both Ostrogradsky's approach and Dirac's algorithm for constrained systems. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian treatment of the perfect fluid is based on Schutz's formalism. Second, we postulate the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and investigate its solutions both analytically and numerically. For radiation we are led to a system of fractional differential equations for which we use Caputo fractional derivative operator. We construct wave packets in momentum space, with the fluid's variable acting as external time parameter.

hep-th.title: Resistive alignment of a black-hole magnetosphere
hep-th.author: Ruben Lier, Oliver Porth
hep-th.abstract: Recent numerical simulations have shown that black-hole magnetospheres evolve rapidly toward alignment between the magnetic axis and spin axis but the physical origin of this process has remained unclear. We develop an analytic theory of this alignment within resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Taking the slow-spin Blandford-Znajek monopole solution as the exterior magnetic field, we reduce the induction equation to a relaxation equation for the current-sheet inclination angle. Our analysis shows that alignment results from second-order spin effects in the Blandford-Znajek solution combined with explicit resistive dissipation. We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and find a regime in which the measured late-time secular decay agrees quantitatively with the analytic prediction.

hep-th.title: Chiral Symmetries in the Standard Model of Particle Physics and its Extensions
hep-th.author: Sergio Ferrando Solera
hep-th.abstract: Chiral gauge theories are a central focus of research in theoretical particle physics due to the parity symmetry breaking observed in the Standard Model. Left-Right Symmetric Models (LRM) explain the breaking of parity through a Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism, predicting new $W_R$ and $Z_R$ gauge bosons. The absence of direct BSM physics detection at the LHC has driven research towards precision observables and Effective Field Theories (EFTs), particularly the SMEFT framework. Precision radiative calculations in chiral theories using dimensional regularization require a $D$-dimensional $\gamma_5$ prescription, such as the mathematically consistent Breitenlohner-Maison-'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. However, this scheme introduces gauge symmetry-breaking terms that obstruct Slavnov-Taylor identities. A primary objective of this thesis is to provide a pedagogical introduction to cancelling these spurious anomalies via algebraic renormalization, and to derive the one-loop symmetry-restoring finite counterterms required to renormalize the four-fermion operators of the $\nu$SMEFT. Furthermore, the thesis explores UV completions like LRMs embedded in other BSM theories like the Grand Unified Theories. This embedding implies that no discrete symmetries remain at the TeV scale and allows LRMs to be treated as EFTs with the minimal scalar content needed to perform the Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism. The second main objective is to derive robust lower bounds on the masses of the new gauge bosons and the LR scale using collider observables. This analysis is performed for both the effective and traditional LRMs, ensuring that the results are independent of other parameters of the theory.

hep-th.title: The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion
hep-th.author: Vitor Cardoso, Jose María Ezquiaga, Julio Parra-Martinez, Laura Sberna, Gustavo J. Turiaci, Lieke van Son
hep-th.abstract: Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise other breakthrough discoveries that the next generation of scientists will need to interpret. The School on Gravity (22--26 June 2026, Copenhagen) aimed to introduce junior scientists--graduate students and advanced undergraduates with a background in general relativity--to a wide range of foundational topics in the exciting new field of gravitational-wave physics. Topics spanned from the theory of motion, to new challenges introduced by quantum physics, to the astrophysics of black holes and source modeling for gravitational-wave detectors. The School on Gravity took place at the legendary Auditorium A of the Niels Bohr Institute, inviting students and lecturers to challenge current paradigms in gravitational physics in the spirit of the quantum revolution that unfolded in this very room. These lecture notes aim at opening up those new ideas presented in Auditorium A to the rest of the scientific community.

hep-th.title: Relaxation Dark Energy: Compositional Dynamics and the Future of Cosmic Acceleration
hep-th.author: Gianmassimo Tasinato
hep-th.abstract: If cosmic acceleration is driven by a positive cosmological constant, the universe approaches an eternally accelerating de Sitter state, whose interpretation in quantum gravity remains elusive. We develop a framework in which acceleration is instead a transient stage of dark-sector relaxation towards compositional equilibrium: matter and dark energy approach a stationary density ratio, eventually diluting like pressureless matter. Guided by linear response theory and Onsager's near-equilibrium regression hypothesis, we describe this evolution through a composition variable measuring departure from equilibrium. Extending constant fractional relaxation to the full background evolution yields the dark-energy equation of state $w=w_0a^{-n}$, where $n$ is the relaxation rate per e-fold of expansion. This history connects early dark-energy suppression, an upward phantom crossing and a density maximum to a pressureless scaling future. Using DESI DR2 BAO and Planck distance priors, with and without three alternative supernova compilations, we find a nominal $2.6$--$3.6\sigma$ preference for nonzero relaxation over constant $w$. The composition framework also motivates a constitutive prescription for linear perturbations that remains regular at phantom crossing. Near equilibrium, regular long-wavelength composition disturbances relax at the background rate to leading order, while small-scale fluctuations propagate as damped sound waves. We prove, however, that for separately conserved matter and dark energy, the pointwise constitutive relation cannot sustain a regular, gradient-stable negative-pressure branch throughout its full past evolution. We explore modifications of the pressure response and their consistency with neighbouring homogeneous histories, identifying requirements for extending the near-equilibrium description to the full cosmological evolution.

hep-th.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
hep-th.author: J. Gurzó, G. Fejős
hep-th.abstract: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

hep-th.title: Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
hep-th.author: Pramod Padmanabhan, Somnath Maity, Akash Sinha, Vladimir Korepin
hep-th.abstract: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.

hep-th.title: Evidence of Taste-Symmetry restoration for Kähler-Dirac fermions on Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations
hep-th.author: Mingwei Dai, Walter Freeman, Mason Grieb, Jack Laiho, Marc Schiffer, Judah Unmuth-Yockey
hep-th.abstract: We study the spectrum of two-particle bound states of Kähler-Dirac fermions coupled via gravity in Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations (EDT). We work in the quenched approximation, where the geometry is allowed to fluctuate, but there is no back-reaction from the matter on the geometry. The Kähler-Dirac action respects an exact $U(1)$ symmetry that is related to continuum chiral symmetry, and this $U(1)$ symmetry ensures that some of the bound-state masses vanish in the chiral limit of vanishing fermion bare mass. The bound-state masses that are not protected by the $U(1)$ symmetry do not vanish in the chiral limit, but the scale associated with the symmetry breaking does not appear to be a physical scale like the Planck mass or the curvature scale of the emergent de Sitter background. Rather, the mass scale associated with this non-degeneracy appears to be a positive power of the lattice spacing, decreasing as the continuum limit is approached. This suggests that Kähler-Dirac fermions in EDT can be interpreted as the gravity analog of staggered fermions in flat-space lattice field theories, with similar behavior.

hep-th.title: An exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
hep-th.author: A. A. Araújo Filho
hep-th.abstract: We construct an exact stationary axisymmetric vacuum configuration in metric affine Kalb-Ramond gravity with zero cosmological constant. Independent variation of the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field yields the complete field equations and the algebraic relation between the physical and auxiliary geometries. A Kerr auxiliary metric and a closed corotating vacuum two form of fixed positive norm determine the physical metric. The tensor kernel contains the horizon generator, and the metrics, independent connection, and vacuum field share a smooth extension across the nonextremal physical Killing horizon and the rotation axes at finite radius for unequal deformation factors. We obtain an explicit sufficient domain for a causal exterior and an asymptotically locally flat end at fixed nonpolar angles. The physical Hamiltonian yields the timelike and null equations, equatorial effective potentials, circular orbit properties, radial stability, and perihelion advance. Numerical photon evolution determines the critical curve on an orthonormal observer screen. Its size, shape, and centroid depend on $\epsilon=\xi_2b^2/[2(1+\xi_1b^2)]$ at fixed normalized mass scale and spin, with Kerr recovered at $\epsilon=0$. Geometric observations probe this combination and retain an exact degeneracy between the curvature couplings. A static equatorial comparison with Mercury gives a conditional sensitivity of $2.30\times10^{-11}$ for $|2\epsilon|$ under the stated angular convention and mass setting.

hep-th.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
hep-th.author: Oliver H. E. Philcox
hep-th.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $\sigma_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

hep-th.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
hep-th.author: Seung J. Lee, Taewook Youn
hep-th.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

hep-th.title: Regular and Floquet bases for gauge and gravity theories: a non perturbative approach
hep-th.author: Davide Fioravanti, Marco Rossi
hep-th.abstract: This paper presents physical interpretations of the change of basis in Heun-type equations (Heun's and their confluences and reductions) from solutions decaying at two singular points to Floquet solutions. A crucial element in these connection relations is the phase acquired by Floquet solutions when transitioning between (ir)regular singularities. We exploit a novel `kink method' to compute the quantum momentum of the solutions as convergent series, explicitly at all orders. Consequently, by integrating the Floquet solutions term by term, the acquired phase can be explicitly derived as a series as well. Given that Heun equations and their confluences describe ${\cal N}=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theories in the Nekrasov-Shatashvili (NS) background (corresponding to the quantization of Seiberg-Witten differentials) as well as black hole perturbation theory, tests and predictions can be established in both domains. Specifically, we perform a critical verification matching the acquired phase with the dual gauge period, $A_D$. On the gravity side, our explicit and systematic results agree with standard methods used to analyse the Teukolsky or Regge-Wheeler equations. This procedure provides an effective alternative to instanton and gravity computations. Ultimately, it marks the initial steps toward establishing a dictionary between integrability and gravitational quantities.

hep-th.title: A Note on the Feynman Lectures on Gravitation
hep-th.author: Satoshi Nakajima
hep-th.abstract: Following Feynman's lectures on gravitation, we consider the theory of the gravitational (massless spin-2) field in flat spacetime and present the third- and fourth-order Lagrangian densities for the gravitational field. In particular, we present detailed calculations for the third-order Lagrangian density. We point out that the expression for the third-order Lagrangian density which Feynman provided is not a solution of Feynman's condition that the third-order Lagrangian density must satisfy. However, Feynman's third-order Lagrangian density gives the correct perihelion shift.

hep-th.title: Euclidean Correlation Functions in Quantum Gravity
hep-th.author: Jack Laiho, Kenny Ratliff
hep-th.abstract: We calculate Euclidean correlation functions through next-to-leading order in the low energy effective theory of gravity. We focus on correlation functions of curvature and volume operators, calculating these functions through one-loop order. We show that quantum fluctuations of the background spacetime must be taken into account in order to obtain gauge invariant expressions, and we point out a subtlety associated with the analytic continuation of the conformal mode. Our final expressions for the correlation functions involve only Newton's constant and the source-sink separation, and they are a universal prediction of the low energy effective theory. Thus, they serve as a useful point of comparison for nonperturbative lattice formulations of gravity.

hep-th.title: Nonaxisymmetric (2+1) black holes with Dym boundary conditions
hep-th.author: Miguel Pino, Francisco Reyes
hep-th.abstract: We present the spectrum of stationary black hole solutions associated with the first nontrivial member of the Dym family of boundary conditions. The analysis combines the holonomy conditions provided by the Chern-Simons formulation of AdS$_3$ gravity with the periodic solutions of the stationary Dym equation. The resulting spacetimes are characterized by two positive real parameters, two positive integers, and a relative phase, generically describing stationary, nonaxisymmetric black holes.

hep-th.title: Linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal supergravity in the harmonic approach
hep-th.author: Evgeny Ivanov, Nikita Zaigraev
hep-th.abstract: Using the harmonic superspace approach, we construct the superconformal harmonic action for $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl supermultiplet. The fundamental objects of the theory are unconstrained analytic potentials $h^{++\alpha\dot{\alpha}}, h^{++\alpha+}, h^{++\dot{\alpha}+}, h^{(+4)}$, which distinguishes our construction among the previously known ones. An important role is played by the ``half-analyticity'' conditions introduced inarXiv:2407.08524[hep-th]. The structure of the harmonic linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action to large extent repeats the structure of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action, which suggests a conjecture on the possible structure of the complete nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl theory action in the harmonic superspace. We provide a detailed study of the rigid superconformal properties of the proposed action and prove its invariance in both harmonic and chiral superspaces. First steps are also undertaken towards constructing the nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action, based on an analogy with $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action just mentioned and a generalization of the concept of half-analyticity to curved harmonic superspace.

hep-th.title: A structural criterion for asymptotic states in Supersymmetry
hep-th.author: Stefano Bellucci, Stefania De Matteo
hep-th.abstract: The occurrence of a field in a quantum field theory does not by itself establish the existence of a corresponding asymptotic particle. We formulate a structural criterion separating operator admissibility, dynamical spectral realization, and particlehood, using the exterior-polynomial classification of gravitino mass bilinears as a prototype. Particlehood is organized as an ordered filtration of geometry and state, effective algebra, dynamics, and spectral analysis, with the localization criterion $\Lambda[\Psi]$ defined by the presence of a physical spectral atom of non-zero weight. We obtain four results. First, conventional linearly realized global supercharges are obstructed on a positive-definite de Sitter Hilbert space when the full diagonal odd--odd bracket satisfies a positivity-reversal condition; the spacetime part is shown to be reversible in $\mathfrak{so}(4,1)$, while internal generators require a separate check. Second, invariant scalar de Sitter product decompositions remove the Minkowski additive two-particle threshold in principal-series channels. Third, a spectral-transfer decomposition shows how continuum weight in a mediator propagator can open absorptive support for an external field below the atomic mediator threshold. Fourth, in a reduced effective-operator basis, the fermionic vector derivative coupling is redundant under current-conservation assumptions, whereas the axial dimension-five coupling is physical unless excluded by parity or CP; under that symmetry hypothesis the residual fermionic derivative potential starts one operator dimension above the scalar one. Exact unbroken supersymmetry enforces multiplet rigidity of the atomic criterion.

hep-th.title: Loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime: The parity-split IBP system and $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations
hep-th.author: Jiaqi Chen, Bo Feng, Zhehan Qin, Yi-Xiao Tao
hep-th.abstract: We develop integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals of cosmological correlators in de Sitter (dS) spacetime, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We identify a structural property of the dS IBP system: for an $n$-propagator family, it splits into $2^n$ closed subsystems classified by the parity of the propagator indices. We further formulate a Baikov representation for loop integrals in dS space and derive the corresponding dimensional recurrence relations. In flat spacetime, intersection theory shows that $\mathrm{d}\log$-form master integrands lead to $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations. Motivated by fibration intersection theory, we conjecture that this construction extends to dS integrands involving Hankel functions. We verify this conjecture in the one-loop bubble family and determine the associated alphabet.

hep-th.title: de Sitter in String Theory vs. Gibbons & Hawking
hep-th.author: Yoav Zigdon
hep-th.abstract: This paper corroborates a statement that perturbative string theory does not admit a solution whose spacetime metric is de Sitter times a closed manifold, to all orders in the $\alpha'$ and $g_s$ expansions, under the assumption that the logarithm of the sphere partition function of Euclidean quantum gravity receives a nonzero contribution proportional to $\frac{1}{G_N}$ in a saddle-point approximation. This assumption is related to the Gibbons-Hawking proposal that the entropy of the cosmological horizon of the static patch is $\frac{A}{4G_N}$. Evidence for the statement comes from independent approaches to the effective action of string theory, all of which agree that the tree-level action vanishes for closed Euclidean target-space solutions. One possible implication is that the state of the Universe will depart from an asymptotically de Sitter spacetime.

hep-th.title: Probing black holes with equivariant localization
hep-th.author: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Christopher Couzens, Alice Lüscher
hep-th.abstract: We introduce equivariant localization as a method for computing the action of probe branes in supergravity backgrounds. We apply it to supersymmetric probe D3-branes in type IIB supersymmetric spacetimes obtained by uplifting the Kerr-Newman-AdS$_5$ black hole on a toric Sasaki-Einstein space. Depending on the cycles they wrap, such branes represent non-perturbative corrections to or defect operator insertions in the superconformal index of a large family of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ quiver superconformal field theories. The resulting action reduces to equivariant integrals and can be evaluated entirely from toric data.

hep-th.title: The Free Particle--Oscillator--Inverted Oscillator Triangle: Conformal Bridges, Metaplectic Rotations and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ Structure
hep-th.author: Andrey Alcala, Mikhail S. Plyushchay
hep-th.abstract: We study the free particle (FP), harmonic oscillator (HO) and inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO) as parabolic, elliptic and hyperbolic realizations of one conformal/metaplectic structure. Within this framework, we develop a common free-particle construction of HO bound and coherent states and IHO resonance and scattering data. The construction extends the FP--HO conformal bridge to both hyperbolic orientations using real metaplectic rotations through $\pm\pi/4$. These rotations map $2\Omega D$ to $\mp H_{\rm IHO}$ and carry the FP threshold Jordan module into the two Gamow families. Applied to Fourier characters, they give light-cone generating states whose Taylor and Mellin decompositions recover resonance and real-energy connection data, respectively. The familiar IHO scattering amplitudes and their Gamma-function poles thereby enter the same construction. We identify the crossed roles of the elliptic and hyperbolic generators in the two stationary bridges and develop the hyperbolic Cayley--Niederer map as their time-dependent counterpart. The $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ extension keeps track of the two parity sectors and the linear generating operators. A phase-space analysis reconciles exact Liouville transport with nonzero stationary transmission, distinguishing asymptotic quantum currents from classical trajectories across separatrices. We also briefly discuss applications of the common quadratic structure to barrier scattering, time-dependent oscillators and quantum fields in gravitational backgrounds.

hep-th.title: Boundary Energy Density and Null Propagation in Global AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
hep-th.author: Shiki Yoshikawa
hep-th.abstract: We study how bulk propagation in global AdS$_3$ is reflected in boundary energy densities of the dual CFT$_2$ on the cylinder. A key feature of the global geometry, which is absent in the Poincaré-patch description, is that a null excitation emitted from the boundary reaches the antipodal boundary point after $\Delta\tau=\pi$ and returns to the original boundary point after $\Delta\tau=2\pi$. We show that the CFT energy density reproduces this sequence through two chiral peaks that move along the boundary light-cone directions, meet at the antipodal point, and return to the original point after one global period. For a wave-packet state, the leading energy density consists of two chiral peaks moving along the boundary light-cone directions; their relative weights encode the impact parameter of the corresponding bulk null ray. For a state constructed from an operator of large conformal dimension with a Euclidean time regulator (LCD state), the exact cylinder stress tensor gives two periodic chiral pulses moving along the boundary light-cone directions. These pulses reach the antipodal point and return to the original point at the same global times as the radial null geodesic in the bulk. Thus the boundary energy density provides a time-dependent boundary profile that reflects characteristic global features of null propagation in AdS$_3$.

hep-th.title: Novel $\mathcal{N}=2$ higher-spin supercurrents
hep-th.author: Nikita Zaigraev
hep-th.abstract: We study cubic interactions of $\mathcal N=2$ massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace. We construct the complete class of abelian $(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s_1},\mathbf{s_2})$ cubic vertices with the minimal number of space-time derivatives. Such vertices exist only for $\mathbf{s}\geq \mathbf{s_1}+\mathbf{s_2}$ and universally take the form of the gauge prepotential coupled to the conserved higher-spin supercurrent. For~$\mathbf{s_1}\neq\mathbf{s_2}$, we find the novel complex principal supercurrent, whose real and imaginary parts generate the parity-invariant and the parity-breaking interactions, respectively. The supercurrents are constructed from gauge-invariant $\mathcal N=2$ higher-spin Weyl supertensors associated with the spin-$\mathbf{s_1}$ and spin-$\mathbf{s_2}$ gauge multiplets. These supertensors are defined in terms of unconstrained higher-spin analytic prepotentials. We also derive the complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents associated with the $(s,s_1,s_2)$ vertices, including both traceless currents and currents with the non-vanishing trace.

hep-th.title: Fire at the Tip of the Throat: Hagedorn Phase after brane-antibrane inflation?
hep-th.author: Dibya Chakraborty, Ahmed Rakin Kamal
hep-th.abstract: We study the post-inflationary open-string Hagedorn phase in perturbatively moduli stabilized brane-antibrane inflation. In this class of models, the volume modulus is stabilized by perturbative corrections rather than by non-perturbative effects to the superpotential, thereby avoiding the standard brane-antibrane $\eta$-problem. Since inflation ends through tachyon condensation and brane-antibrane annihilation, the endpoint is intrinsically stringy and need not be described immediately by an ordinary radiation bath. We analyze whether the energy released at annihilation can drive the visible sector into an open-string Hagedorn phase, and study the consequences for dark radiation. If the Standard Model (SM) branes lie in the same throat as where the annihilation occurs, we find that a modest fraction of the released energy deposited into surviving visible open strings is sufficient to enter the Hagedorn regime and can suppress the effective number of relativistic species $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ below current observational bounds. If the SM lies in a different throat, the result depends on inter-throat energy transfer: prompt or delayed transfer can still yield a visible Hagedorn phase. However, the mechanism is most efficient when the local string scale in the SM throat is lower than or comparable to that in the annihilation throat.

hep-th.title: Oscillon Floquet Modes and the Operators that Excite Them
hep-th.author: Bilguun Bayarsaikhan, Jarah Evslin, Sujoy Mahato
hep-th.abstract: We present the scattering modes of the oscillon, to the first three orders in the Fodor expansion, in terms of elementary functions. In the case of relativistic modes, these results are new. We use them to fully decompose the field and also to analytically invert the decomposition. In quantum field theory, this allows us to show that the corresponding creation and annihilation operators satisfy the usual oscillator algebra, extending to relativistic modes the demonstration that, at a fixed order in the Fodor expansion, a periodic oscillon state exists.

hep-th.title: Energy-Energy Correlators at Strong Coupling
hep-th.author: Max Jackson, Lecheng Ren, Bo Wang, Congkao Wen
hep-th.abstract: We study energy-energy correlators (EEC) in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory at strong 't Hooft coupling $\lambda$. We consider the EEC in states created by half-BPS operators of arbitrary dimension $p$, and determine the corresponding event-shape function up to order $\lambda^{-3/2}$ from the worldsheet representation of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude with Kaluza-Klein external states. For $p=2$ we compute the second curvature correction, which completes the EEC through order $\lambda^{-2}$; the new contribution improves the agreement with recently derived non-perturbative bounds at intermediate coupling. We further develop a complementary method in which the strong-coupling expansion coefficients of the EEC are extracted directly from the Wilson coefficients of low-energy expansion of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, and find the two approaches in perfect agreement.

hep-th.title: Color-Kinematics Duality and the Double Copy in Curved Spacetimes
hep-th.author: Mariana Carrillo González
hep-th.abstract: The double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. This review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. After recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in AdS, dS, and other non-trivial backgrounds. We then review classical and field-level maps, including Kerr--Schild, Weyl, Cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. A separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. Throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.

hep-th.title: Stress-Testing Swampland Bounds with Class S Theories
hep-th.author: Gabriel Fenati, Miguel Montero, Irene Valenzuela
hep-th.abstract: We test the Sharpened Distance Conjecture (SharpDC) for CFTs, as well as the Refined Distance Conjecture (RDC), in AdS$_5$ gravitational spacetimes, using the CFT dual. The former provides a lower bound on the exponential mass decay rate of the tower of states becoming light at infinite distance in the conformal manifold, while the latter bounds the bulk field range that can be traversed before the exponential behaviour of the tower kicks in. We prove the SharpDC for any large $N$ Lagrangian supersymmetric gauge theory with a finite number $M$ of gauge factors and vanishing one-loop $\beta$-function. We also investigate whether it universally holds in the limits of large central charge, finding that it does not: We exhibit concrete examples in Class S theories where the conjecture is violated in the $M\rightarrow\infty$ limit with $N$ fixed, where the size of the bulk internal geometry is much larger than the AdS curvature scale. We also test the RDC in the moduli space of Class S theories without punctures in the large $N$ limit, showing that it amounts to a precise upper bound on the Weil-Petersson diameter of the moduli space of Riemann surfaces of genus $g$. This bound is consistent with all the mathematical literature up to date, but so far remains unproven.

hep-th.title: An attempt to derive the LVS from a 10d EFT perspective
hep-th.author: Arthur Hebecker, Andreas Schachner, Gaetano Maria Sifo
hep-th.abstract: Non-perturbative scalar potentials are a central ingredient for stabilising moduli in flux compactifications. A key target in this context is the direct 10d derivation of the LVS AdS potential, i.e., the scalar potential of the Large Volume Scenario before the uplift. The familiar result, relying on 4d supergravity machinery and large volume expansion, consists of three terms of parametric form $\exp(-2a\tau_s)/{\mathcal V}$, $W_0\exp(-a\tau_s)/{\mathcal V}^2$, and $W_0^2/{\mathcal V}^3$. In plain 10d EFT language, the first term is an instanton-anti-instanton effect while the second term comes from a single instanton coupled to 3-form flux. When attempting to derive the suppression by the volume ${\mathcal V}$ directly from the 10d EFT, one encounters a puzzle: One expects a flux-dilution factor $1/\sqrt{\mathcal V}$ for the second term and a factor $1/{\mathcal V}^2$ from Weyl rescaling to the 4d Einstein frame for both the first and second term. Thus, the total volume suppression for these two terms is stronger than in the aforementioned 4d EFT expectations. We discuss the underlying logic in detail, also in the gaugino condensation case, but fail to find a satisfactory explanation for the mismatch. While log-corrections to the Kähler potential may be responsible, these would have to be strong enough to affect the outcome of the LVS scheme at the ${\mathcal O}(1)$ level. What is worse, the origin of the required correction remains unclear.

hep-th.title: Bulk OPE Coefficients of the $E$-Series Virasoro Minimal Models
hep-th.author: Amaury Lhoste, Jiaxin Qiao, Masahito Yamazaki
hep-th.abstract: We present bulk-primary operator-product coefficients for every Virasoro minimal model with an $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$ modular invariant. Dividing by a universal product of chiral generalized-minimal-model OPE coefficients reduces the conformal bootstrap problem to a finite algebraic problem governed by root-of-unity quantum-group $6j$ symbols. The exceptional factors of the OPE coefficients can be chosen independent of the second Kac indices $s$, and their dependence on the central charge reduces to finitely many reference cases and explicit phases. A finite computer-assisted calculation yields candidate algebraic $s=1$ seed data and high-precision numerical evidence for existence and uniqueness modulo primary-field signs. We prove that exact existence and uniqueness for these seeds imply the corresponding result for all Kac labels within the genus-zero bulk locality and crossing equations; the finite seed step remains uncertified. The three families require $18$, $32$, and $107$ representative reduced OPE coefficients for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, respectively. We provide reconstruction conventions and coefficient tables for both unitary and nonunitary models. Our calculation assumes only Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality (permutation symmetry) and OPE associativity (crossing equations).

hep-th.title: Absence of Continuous Spin Particles in Superstring Theory
hep-th.author: Arwa Alabbasi(1), Fernando Quevedo(1 and 2) ((1) Department of Physics, New York University Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, (2) DAMTP, University of Cambridge, Wilberforce Road, Cambridge, UK)
hep-th.abstract: The study of continuous spin particles, as general low-energy implications of relativity and quantum mechanics, has intensified in recent years with potential experimental signatures. In this note we show that these particles are absent in perturbative super-string theories, generalising a result inarXiv:1302.4771to the supersymmetric case. This stands out as a general low-energy prediction of all perturbative superstring constructions.

hep-th.title: Sharp null-energy lower bounds for Page-like entropy excursions in two-dimensional conformal field theory
hep-th.author: Soufiane Karmoudi, Mohammed Daoud
hep-th.abstract: We derive sharp lower bounds on the energy cost of Page-like entanglement entropy excursions in two-dimensional conformal field theory. For states satisfying the primary quantum null energy condition (QNEC), the positive null energy $E_+$ obeys a sharp lower bound with two branches separated by the threshold $\Delta S=(c/6)\ln 2$. We also derive a sharp lower bound on the net energy $E_{\rm net}$, with a coefficient larger by a factor of two than the value quoted by Abdolrahimi and Page [Phys. Rev. D 92, 083005 (2015)] and, in the QNEC-saturating sector, we obtain a sharp lower bound on the negative energy $E_-$. The constants are sharp as infima over smooth conformal vacua. We determine the entropy profiles that minimize $E_+$ for general QNEC states and the one that minimizes $E_-$ in the saturating sector. Finally, for an excursion containing an infinite sequence of small sub-excursions within a finite duration, we derive a necessary condition for the total positive energy to remain finite, which is stronger than requiring the entropy to have finite total variation.

hep-th.title: Proof of a Universal Speed Limit on Fast Scrambling in Quantum Systems
hep-th.author: Amit Vikram, Laura Shou, Victor Galitski
hep-th.abstract: We prove that the time required for sustained information scrambling in any Hamiltonian quantum system is universally at least logarithmic in the entanglement entropy of scrambled states. This addresses two foundational problems in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics. (1) It sets the earliest possible time for the applicability of equilibrium statistical mechanics in a quantum system coupled to a bath at a finite temperature. (2) It proves a version of the fast scrambling conjecture, originally motivated in models associated with black holes, as a fundamental property of quantum mechanics itself. Our result builds on a refinement of the energy-time uncertainty principle in terms of the infinite temperature spectral form factor in quantum chaos. We generalize this formulation to arbitrary initial states of the bath, including finite temperature states, by mapping Hamiltonian dynamics with any initial state to nonunitary dynamics at infinite temperature. A regularized spectral form factor emerges naturally from this procedure, whose decay is universally constrained by analyticity in complex time. This establishes an exact speed limit on information scrambling by the most general quantum mechanical Hamiltonian, without any restrictions on locality or the nature of interactions.

hep-th.title: Proof of a magnificent conjecture
hep-th.author: M. Kool, J.V. Rennemo
hep-th.abstract: Motivated by super-Yang-Mills theory on a Calabi-Yau 4-fold, Nekrasov and Piazzalunga have assigned weights to $r$-tuples of solid partitions and conjectured a formula for their weighted generating function.We define $K$-theoretic virtual invariants of Quot schemes of 0-dimensional quotients of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^4}^{\oplus r}$ by realizing them as zero loci of isotropic sections of orthogonal bundles on non-commutative Quot schemes. Via the Oh-Thomas localization formula, we recover Nekrasov-Piazzalunga's weights and derive their sign rule.Our proof passes through refining the $K$-theoretic invariants to sheaves and describing them via Clifford modules, which lets us show that they arise from a factorizable sequence of sheaves in the sense of Okounkov. Taking limits of the equivariant parameters, we then deduce the Nekrasov-Piazzalunga conjecture from its 3-dimensional analog.

hep-th.title: Quark and lepton mixing in the asymptotically safe Standard Model
hep-th.author: Astrid Eichhorn, Zois Gyftopoulos, Aaron Held
hep-th.abstract: The quark mixing (CKM) matrix is near-diagonal, whereas the lepton mixing (PMNS) matrix is not. We learn that both observations can generically be explained within an ultraviolet completion of the Standard Model with gravity. This ultraviolet completion results in approximate relations between CKM matrix elements. The accuracy with which these hold translates into the length of asymptotically safe scaling regimes. Experimental data are consistent with the theoretical expectations arising from a fixed-point cascade at transplanckian scales. Similar results would hold for the PMNS matrix if neutrino Yukawa couplings were large. The ultraviolet complete theory, therefore, must -- and in fact can -- avoid such an outcome. It achieves this through a dynamical mechanism that limits the size of neutrino Yukawa couplings. Thus, large neutrino mixing is intimately tied to small Dirac neutrino masses, $\sum m_{\nu} \lesssim O(1)\, \rm eV$, and a mass gap in the Standard Model fermion masses.

hep-th.title: Anomalies of global symmetries on the lattice
hep-th.author: Yi-Ting Tu, David M. Long, Dominic V. Else
hep-th.abstract: 't Hooft anomalies of global symmetries play a fundamental role in quantum many-body systems and quantum field theory (QFT). In this paper, we make a systematic analysis of lattice anomalies - the analog of 't Hooft anomalies in lattice systems - for which we give a precise definition. Crucially, a lattice anomaly is not a feature of a specific Hamiltonian, but rather is a topological invariant of the symmetry action. The controlled setting of lattice systems allows for a systematic and rigorous treatment of lattice anomalies, shorn of the technical challenges of QFT. We find that lattice anomalies reproduce the expected properties of QFT anomalies in many ways, but also have crucial differences. In particular, lattice anomalies and QFT anomalies are not, contrary to a common expectation, in one-to-one correspondence, and there can be nontrivial anomalies on the lattice that are infrared (IR) trivial: They admit symmetric trivial gapped ground states, and map to trivial QFT anomalies at low energies. Nevertheless, we show that lattice anomalies (including IR-trivial ones) have a number of interesting consequences in their own right, including connections to commuting projector models, phases of many-body localized (MBL) systems, and quantum cellular automata (QCA). We make substantial progress on the classification of lattice anomalies and develop several theoretical tools to characterize their consequences on symmetric Hamiltonians. Our work places symmetries of quantum many-body lattice systems into a unified theoretical framework and may also suggest new perspectives on symmetries in QFT.

hep-th.title: Stability of Vacuum and Quantum Dynamics in Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
hep-th.author: Shi-Yuan Li, Chengwu Liu
hep-th.abstract: Canonical quantization on scalar and Maxwell fields is studied for the stability of vacuum and construction of quantum dynamics in Anti-de Sitter spacetimes. The $\xi R\phi^2$ term in the Lagrangian of scalar field with $\xi > 5/48$ (mass term just introduces shift of $\xi$) can cause the spectrum of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian with negative value not bounded from below. The degrees of freedom corresponding to the negative values are constrained system and are ambiguous in space direction and in commutation relation. The only other algebra accommodated in 3-dimensional space consistent with locality, the anti-commutation relation, is definite confronting the constrain, and trivialize the negative spectrum to be inactive and absent degrees of freedom. Thus only the physical bosons corresponding to the non-negative spectrum span the Hilbert space. For the Maxwell fields as another constrained system, the gauge invariant canonical energy momentum tensor straightforwardly leads to the gauge invariant non-negative Hamiltonian. The 2-dimensional independent dynamical degrees of freedom are quantized in temporal gauge. The energy momentum tensors for both quantized fields are renormalized to be finite at operator level, which guarantee the stable vacuum maximally symmetric and the particle Fock states the representation of the AdS symmetry SO(2,3). Adopting Weinberg's framework, the new covariant free quantum scalar field is reconstructed in the corresponding mode function space isomorphic to the free boson Hilbert space, allowing various local effective interaction terms among fields introduced. The Yang-Feldman equations relate the free fields and the interacting fields with the Green functions determined properly in the mode function space.

hep-th.title: Generalized First Law and Smarr-type Relation: Beyond Additivity and Extensivity
hep-th.author: Usman Zafar, Krishnakanta Bhattacharya, Kazuharu Bamba
hep-th.abstract: In this work, we develop a general framework for deriving the first law of black hole thermodynamics and the associated Smarr-type relation for 4-dimensional static spherically symmetric spacetimes within a broad class of generalized entropy models. In addition, by employing the entropy representation for the Reissner--Nordström (RN) black hole, we determine a concise curvature functional that depends only on this representation and its derivatives. A general flatness condition is derived, demonstrating that when the entropy Hessian metric is regular and nondegenerate, both homogeneous power-law transformations and a separate logarithmic branch leave the RN black hole's Ruppeiner geometry flat. On the other hand, Rényi, Sharma-Mittal, Kaniadakis, and LQG-inspired entropy deformations typically give rise to nonvanishing curvature in the regular thermodynamic regime, demonstrating that the extremality of the RN black hole does not by itself require a curvature divergence.

hep-th.title: On the magnetic counterpart of the Uehling correction
hep-th.author: T. Azevedo, F.A. Barone, C. Farina, R. de Melo e Souza, G. Zarpelon
hep-th.abstract: In this work, we investigate the magnetic properties of the quantum vacuum in the context of QED. We calculate the quantum relativistic correction of virtual particle-anti-particle pair creation to the field of a classical point-like idealized magnet. Using such correction, we find the induced currents stemming from the effect of the polarization of the vacuum, which behaves like a paramagnetic medium. We also calculate the correction to the electric dipole potential and show that the well-known symmetry between the classical fields of point electric and magnetic dipoles is broken at the quantum level. Lastly, to illustrate possible applications of our findings, we briefly discuss the effect of the corrections obtained here in the context of neutron-neutron scattering and the hyperfine splitting for hydrogen-like atoms.

hep-th.title: Positive Geometries from Cubic Surfaces
hep-th.author: Bernd Sturmfels, Simon Telen
hep-th.abstract: We present a study of cubic surfaces from the novel perspective of positive geometry. Our positive geometries have dimension two (the surface minus its 27 lines), dimension three (its complement in 3-space), and dimension four (the moduli space). In each case we explore the positive arrangement, its combinatorial rank, and the canonical forms.

hep-th.title: Real versus Complex Fermion Bare Mass and Multi-Wall String Defect Annihilation
hep-th.author: Utsav Atta, Tathagata Ghosh, Sudip Manna
hep-th.abstract: Particle physics models beyond the Standard Model often contain global symmetries to address various unanswered questions. However, a common criticism of theories based on global symmetries is that such symmetries are generally expected to be explicitly violated by gravitational effects at the Planck scale. In the case of a global $U(1)$ symmetry, this explicit breaking can reduce the symmetry to a discrete subgroup of $U(1)$, leading to the formation of cosmic strings attached to multiple domain walls (DWs). These DWs are usually cosmologically problematic, since their slow scaling behavior can eventually dominate the energy density of the Universe, giving rise to the well-known cosmological DW problem, which is strongly constrained by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. In this work, we propose a mechanism for the annihilation of these DWs. If a fermion coupled to the symmetry-breaking scalar has a small bare mass, radiative corrections generate a temperature-dependent vacuum bias that drives DW collapse. As an example, we consider a majoron model with right-handed neutrinos, where gravity-induced operators produce a string-wall network. We show that a real bare Majorana mass is sufficient to induce complete DW annihilation for even-dimensional gravity-induced operators, whereas odd-dimensional operators require a complex bare Majorana mass whose phase lifts the residual vacuum degeneracy, enabling complete annihilation.

hep-th.title: Particle production from bubble collisions
hep-th.author: Anish Ghoshal, Pratyay Pal, Alessandro Strumia
hep-th.abstract: Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.

hep-th.title: Gravitational wave echoes as probes of the maximum mass of strange stars in quadratic curvature-matter coupled gravity
hep-th.author: Debadri Bhattacharjee, Pradip Kumar Chattopadhyay, Kazuharu Bamba
hep-th.abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy provides a powerful avenue for probing exotic compact stars. Recent analyses of GW170817 have reported possible post-merger gravitational wave echoes with a significance of $4.2\sigma$ and a dominant frequency near $72,\text{Hz}$. Such echoes may arise from ultracompact remnants possessing photon spheres that partially trap gravitational perturbations. In general relativity, photon-sphere formation requires the stellar compactness to lie between one-third and four-ninths, a condition difficult to achieve with realistic equations of state. Here, we investigate this possibility in quadratic curvature gravity with non-minimal matter coupling, considering strange stars described by the MIT bag model equation of state. By solving the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we obtain mass-radius relations and identify configurations capable of supporting photon spheres and gravitational wave echoes. The modified Buchdahl limit permits more compact stellar solutions, while photon-sphere constraints restrict the viable parameter space. We find that increasing the bag constant reduces the maximum mass and echo time, shifting the echo frequency toward the kHz regime. The echo constraints impose more stringent maximum mass-radius limits than hydrostatic equilibrium, suggesting revised maximum mass bounds for strange stars. We further compute the critical impact parameter and eikonal quasi-normal modes, demonstrating how modified gravity parameters systematically alter the photon-sphere radius and associated observational signatures. These results establish post-merger strange stars as potential GW echo sources and highlight echoes, optical shadows, and QNMs as complementary probes of modified gravity for next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.
